methods.name: Apply
methods.description:
Create or update an MCP server resource.

 If the resource doesn't exist, creates it. If it exists, updates it.
 The resource is identified by its (scope, org, slug) combination.

methods.name: Create
methods.description:
Create an MCP server resource.

 Returns an error if a resource with the same (scope, org, slug) already exists.
 Use `apply` for idempotent create-or-update semantics.

methods.name: Update
methods.description: Update an existing MCP server resource.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description:
Delete an MCP server resource.

 Permanently removes the MCP server definition.
 Agents referencing this server will need to be updated.

methods.name: UpdateVisibility
methods.description:
Update the visibility of an existing MCP server.

 Only modifies metadata.visibility, leaving spec, status, and other
 metadata fields untouched.

methods.name: Connect
methods.description:
Connect to an MCP server: discover its tools and classify approval policies.

 Connects to the MCP server, enumerates tools and resource templates,
 classifies tool approval policies via a lightweight LLM, and stores the
 results in status.discovered_capabilities and status.tool_approvals.
 Blocks until completion (up to ~30 seconds) and returns the updated McpServer.

methods.name: InitiateOAuthConnect
methods.description:
Start the OAuth authorization flow for an MCP server.

 Performs setup (DCR registration or OAuthApp credential lookup, PKCE
 generation) and returns an authorization URL for the frontend to
 redirect the user to. The frontend calls completeOAuthConnect after
 the user authorizes.

methods.name: CompleteOAuthConnect
methods.description:
Complete the OAuth authorization flow by exchanging the authorization
 code for tokens.

 Called by the frontend after the user is redirected back from the
 OAuth authorization server. Exchanges the code for tokens, stores
 them in the user's personal environment, and creates an OAuthGrant
 record for pre-flight expiry checks.

 After success, the frontend should call connect() to trigger tool
 discovery using the freshly acquired token.

methods.name: DisconnectOAuth
methods.description:
Disconnect the authenticated user's OAuth connection for a resource.

 Tears down the user's personal OAuth connection by deleting the
 OAuthGrant and its associated managed environment (which holds the
 access and refresh tokens). The MCP server definition is unchanged —
 only the caller's credentials are removed.

 Other users' connections to the same resource are unaffected.

 Idempotent: returns disconnected=true when a grant was deleted,
 disconnected=false when no grant existed. Never returns an error
 for a missing grant.

methods.name: SetOrgOAuthApp
methods.description:
Create or update an org-level BYOA OAuth app override for a resource.

 Allows an organization to use its own OAuth app credentials instead of
 the platform default. The handler clones the platform OAuthApp template
 (endpoint URLs, scopes) and applies the org-provided client credentials.

 Idempotent: if an override already exists for this resource + org, the
 existing OAuthApp is updated with the new credentials.

methods.name: DeleteOrgOAuthApp
methods.description:
Remove an org-level BYOA override for a resource.

 Deletes the OAuthAppOverride binding and the OAuthApp resource that
 was created for it. After this, the resolution chain falls back to
 the platform default.

 Existing user OAuthGrants that were issued using the org's OAuthApp
 will fail on next token refresh — those users will need to
 re-authenticate using the platform default or a new org override.

methods.name: Get
methods.description: Get an MCP server by its unique identifier.

methods.name: GetByReference
methods.description:
Get an MCP server by reference (scope + org + slug).

 Preferred method for looking up MCP servers by name/slug rather than
 system-generated ID.

methods.name: GetOAuthGrantStatus
methods.description:
Check whether the authenticated user has an active OAuth grant for
 an MCP server in the specified org.

 Returns grant metadata (connected status, token expiry, auth method)
 without exposing any secret token values. The frontend uses this to
 render the correct OAuth state in the MCP server detail page and
 session composer.

methods.name: GetOrgOAuthApp
methods.description:
Query whether an org has a BYOA override for a resource.

 Returns override metadata (existence, OAuthApp ID, client_id) without
 exposing secrets. The frontend uses this to show which credential
 source is active and to offer override management options to org admins.

methodTypes.name: UpdateVisibilityInput
methodTypes.description:
Input for updating the visibility of any API resource.

 Used by resource-specific command controllers to change visibility.
 Each controller's updateVisibility RPC accepts this shared input
 and returns the full updated resource.

 Visibility transitions trigger FGA tuple management in Cloud mode. Each
 level maps to exactly one tuple shape; on a transition the tuple for the
 old level is removed and the tuple for the new level is created:
 - PRIVATE:  no visibility tuple (owner + explicit grants only)
 - ORG:      resource#viewer@organization:<org>#member
 - PUBLIC:   resource#viewer@identity_account:* (gated by allow_public)
 - PLATFORM: resource#platform_viewer@identity_provider:<idp>#platform_user

 Not all resources support all visibility levels — the supported set is
 declared per kind via VisibilityConfig in kind_meta:
 - Blueprints (agent, workflow, skill, mcp_server):
     PRIVATE, ORG, PUBLIC, or PLATFORM
 - Instances (agent_instance, workflow_instance):
     PRIVATE, ORG, or PUBLIC (never PLATFORM — tenant isolation)

 System-managed DEFAULT instances reject visibility updates entirely:
 their access structurally tracks the parent blueprint via the
 default_of FGA relation.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: ID of the resource whose visibility is being updated.

fields.name: Visibility
fields.description:
The new visibility setting for the resource.
 Must not be unspecified (0). Valid values depend on resource kind —
 see the VisibilityConfig in the kind's kind_meta.

methodTypes.name: ConnectInput
methodTypes.description: ConnectInput is the request for the connect RPC.

fields.name: McpServerId
fields.description:
System-generated ID of the MCP server to connect to.
 Obtained from McpServer.metadata.id (e.g., via getByReference).

fields.name: RuntimeEnv
fields.description:
Optional environment variable values for one-time use.
 When empty, values are resolved from the user's personal environment.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization context for credential resolution.

 Used to look up the caller's OAuthGrant and personal environment
 during environment variable resolution. Must match the org used
 during initiateOAuthConnect so the grant composite key aligns.

 Required: the backend rejects the request when this field is empty.

methodTypes.name: InitiateOAuthConnectInput
methodTypes.description:
InitiateOAuthConnectInput starts the OAuth authorization flow for an
 MCP server that has an auth block in its spec.

fields.name: McpServerId
fields.description: System-generated ID of the MCP server to initiate OAuth for.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization context for token storage.
 Tokens are stored in the caller's personal environment within this org.
 Must be an org the caller belongs to.

methodTypes.name: InitiateOAuthConnectOutput
methodTypes.description:
InitiateOAuthConnectOutput contains the authorization URL and metadata
 the frontend needs to redirect the user to the OAuth authorization server.

fields.name: AuthorizationUrl
fields.description:
Full authorization URL to redirect the user to.
 Includes client_id, redirect_uri, code_challenge, state, and scopes.

fields.name: State
fields.description:
Opaque state parameter for CSRF protection.
 The frontend must pass this back in completeOAuthConnect to correlate
 the callback with this initiation.

fields.name: Scopes
fields.description:
OAuth scopes that will be requested.
 For DCR: discovered from authorization server metadata or scope_hints.
 For vendor OAuth: from the OAuthApp spec.

fields.name: ProviderName
fields.description:
Human-readable provider name for UI display during the redirect.
 For DCR: derived from the MCP server name.
 For vendor OAuth: from OAuthApp.spec.provider.

methodTypes.name: CompleteOAuthConnectInput
methodTypes.description:
CompleteOAuthConnectInput finishes the OAuth flow by exchanging the
 authorization code for tokens.

fields.name: McpServerId
fields.description:
System-generated ID of the MCP server.
 Must match the mcp_server_id used in the preceding initiateOAuthConnect.

fields.name: AuthorizationCode
fields.description: Authorization code from the OAuth callback redirect.

fields.name: State
fields.description:
State parameter from the OAuth callback redirect.
 Must match the state returned by initiateOAuthConnect.

methodTypes.name: CompleteOAuthConnectOutput
methodTypes.description:
CompleteOAuthConnectOutput confirms that tokens were successfully
 acquired and stored.

fields.name: Connected
fields.description: Whether the OAuth flow completed successfully and tokens are stored.

fields.name: TargetEnvVar
fields.description:
The environment variable name where the access token was stored.
 Matches McpServerAuth.target_env_var on the MCP server spec.

fields.name: TokenLifetimeHint
fields.description:
Informational hint about expected token lifetime.
 Echoed from McpServerAuth.token_lifetime_hint for UI display.

methodTypes.name: DisconnectOAuthInput
methodTypes.description: DisconnectOAuthInput tears down a user's OAuth connection for a resource.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: System-generated ID of the resource to disconnect OAuth for.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization context. Must match the org used during the original
 OAuth connect flow (part of the OAuthGrant composite key).

methodTypes.name: DisconnectOAuthOutput
methodTypes.description: DisconnectOAuthOutput reports the result of a disconnect request.

fields.name: Disconnected
fields.description:
Whether an active grant was found and deleted.
 true: grant and its managed environment were deleted.
 false: no grant existed for this resource + org + caller. The desired
 state (no OAuth connection) was already achieved. This is not an error.

methodTypes.name: SetOrgOAuthAppInput
methodTypes.description:
SetOrgOAuthAppInput creates or updates an org-level BYOA OAuth app
 override for a resource.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: System-generated ID of the resource to set the BYOA override for.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: Organization that will own this override.

fields.name: ClientId
fields.description: OAuth client ID from the org's own app registration with the vendor.

fields.name: ClientSecret
fields.description:
OAuth client secret from the org's own app registration with the vendor.
 Encrypted at rest, redacted in logs.

methodTypes.name: SetOrgOAuthAppOutput
methodTypes.description: SetOrgOAuthAppOutput confirms the BYOA override was created or updated.

fields.name: OauthAppId
fields.description:
System-generated ID of the OAuthApp resource created (or updated)
 for this override. Can be used to inspect the full OAuthApp via
 OAuthAppQueryController.get.

methodTypes.name: DeleteOrgOAuthAppInput
methodTypes.description: DeleteOrgOAuthAppInput removes an org-level BYOA override for a resource.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: System-generated ID of the resource to remove the override for.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: Organization whose override should be removed.

methodTypes.name: DeleteOrgOAuthAppOutput
methodTypes.description: DeleteOrgOAuthAppOutput confirms the BYOA override was removed.

fields.name: Deleted
fields.description: Whether the delete completed successfully.

methodTypes.name: ApiResourceReference
methodTypes.description:
Generic reference to any API resource by org and slug.
 Used across resources to reference other resources (e.g., Environment, Agent, Skill).
 Canonical format: "org/slug" (e.g., "stigmer/web-search", "acme/my-agent").

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization that owns the referenced resource.

 When non-empty: must be a valid org slug (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens,
 starts with a letter, 1-63 characters). Example: "stigmer", "acme-corp".

 When empty: the reference is relative — the server resolves it to the parent
 resource's organization at write time. All stored and returned references
 always have org populated (absolute form).

 Use empty org for same-org references (the common case).
 Use explicit org for cross-org references (e.g., marketplace resources).

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Kind of the referenced resource (e.g., SKILL, AGENT, MCP_SERVER).

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
Resource slug (user-friendly identifier, unique within org).
 Format: lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, must start with a letter
 and end with a letter or digit (e.g., "web-search", "code-reviewer").
 Length: 2-63 characters.

fields.name: Version
fields.description:
Version of the resource (optional, only applicable to versioned resources like Skills).
 Supports three formats:
 1. Empty/unset → Resolves to "latest" (most recent version)
 2. Tag name → Resolves to version with this tag (e.g., "stable", "v1.0")
 3. Exact hash → Immutable reference to specific version (e.g., "abc123...")

 Default behavior: Empty means "latest" (current version).
 This field is ignored for non-versioned resources.

 Examples:
 - version: ""           → Use latest version
 - version: "latest"     → Use latest version (explicit)
 - version: "stable"     → Use version tagged as "stable"
 - version: "v1.0"       → Use version tagged as "v1.0"
 - version: "abc123..."  → Use exact version with this hash (immutable)

methodTypes.name: GetOAuthGrantStatusInput
methodTypes.description: GetOAuthGrantStatusInput queries the OAuth grant status for a resource.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: System-generated ID of the resource to check grant status for.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization context. Required because the same user can have
 separate OAuth connections for a shared resource across orgs.

methodTypes.name: GetOAuthGrantStatusOutput
methodTypes.description: GetOAuthGrantStatusOutput returns the current OAuth grant status.

fields.name: Connected
fields.description: Whether the user has an active OAuth grant for this resource + org.

fields.name: AccessTokenExpiresAt
fields.description:
When the access token expires (Unix timestamp seconds).
 0 if no grant exists or the token does not expire.

fields.name: TargetEnvVar
fields.description:
The env var name where the access token is stored.
 Empty if no grant exists.

fields.name: AuthMethod
fields.description:
Which auth method was used ("mcp_oauth" or "vendor_oauth").
 Empty if no grant exists.

fields.name: ConnectionHealth
fields.description:
Evaluated health of the OAuth connection.
 Provides an actionable signal beyond the binary "connected" field:
 the frontend can distinguish "healthy" from "expired but refreshable"
 from "expired and needs re-auth" from "never connected."

methodTypes.name: GetOrgOAuthAppInput
methodTypes.description: GetOrgOAuthAppInput queries whether an org has a BYOA override for a resource.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: System-generated ID of the resource to check for an override.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: Organization context to check.

methodTypes.name: GetOrgOAuthAppOutput
methodTypes.description: GetOrgOAuthAppOutput returns the org's BYOA override status.

fields.name: HasOverride
fields.description: Whether an OAuthAppOverride exists for this resource + org.

fields.name: OauthAppId
fields.description:
System-generated ID of the override's OAuthApp.
 Empty when has_override is false.

fields.name: ClientId
fields.description:
Client ID from the override's OAuthApp (non-secret, safe to display).
 Empty when has_override is false. Useful for UI display so the admin
 can verify which app registration is active.

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines whether
 users outside that organization can access the resource.

 The visibility levels map to FGA tuples:
 - PRIVATE: no additional viewer tuples (owner-only access)
 - ORG: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer tuple (everyone in the
   org — the org role hierarchy flows downward, so owners, admins, members
   AND read-only viewers all satisfy the organization#viewer userset)
 - PUBLIC: resource#viewer@identity_account:* with allow_public (all users)
 - PLATFORM: resource#platform_viewer@identity_provider:<idp>#platform_user
   (all members of all organizations managed by the owning org's
   IdentityProvider)

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only the owner, explicitly granted principals, and — for blueprint kinds
 in the cloud edition — org admins can access.
 This is the default for instances and personal resources.

 Org admins count as owners of blueprint kinds (agent, agent_share,
 skill, workflow, project, mcp_server), so a private blueprint stays
 manageable — and visible — to its org's admins. Personal kinds
 (instances, environments, sessions) stay creator-only.

values.name: visibility_public
values.description:
Anyone can access (read) this resource.
 Used for marketplace-published resources (e.g., "stigmer/web-search").
 Write access still requires org membership.
 Named visibility_public to avoid Java reserved keyword conflict.

values.name: visibility_org
values.description:
Everyone in the owning organization can access (read) this resource —
 all org roles including read-only viewers (the role SSO auto-provisioning
 grants by default). Running or otherwise spending against the resource
 still requires the org-level member-or-guest permissions
 (can_create_session / can_create_execution_in); org visibility widens
 read, never spend.
 Used for instances where a team wants shared observability of executions
 without granting access to all authenticated users.

 FGA tuple: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer
 (Before cloud#257 the tuple targeted organization#member, which
 excluded viewer-role users; legacy tuples keep resolving until the
 cloud's boot-time backfill converges them.)

 For workflow instances, this enables zero-tuple-per-execution shared
 observability: everyone in the org sees all executions via inheritance
 once the instance opts in.

values.name: visibility_platform
values.description:
All members of all organizations managed by the owning org's
 IdentityProvider can access (read and execute) this resource.

 "Platform" here means an external platform that operates Stigmer orgs
 on behalf of its own customers (see ManagementMode.platform_managed) —
 NOT the Stigmer platform singleton used by
 AUTHORIZATION_SCOPE_TYPE_PLATFORM.

 This is the "private catalog" primitive for multi-tenant consumers:
 a platform (e.g. Planton) authors blueprints (agents, skills, MCP
 servers, workflows) in its own org and shares them with every child
 org it manages, without exposing them publicly. Child orgs created
 later gain access automatically. Instances, sessions, executions and
 environments are never platform-visible — each child org instantiates
 the shared blueprint inside its own tenant boundary.

 Only valid for blueprint kinds with supports_platform: true, and only
 when the owning org owns at least one IdentityProvider.

 FGA tuple: resource#platform_viewer@identity_provider:<idp>#platform_user

values.name: api_resource_version
values.description: Immutable version record tracking changes to an API resource.

values.name: iam_policy
values.description: Role-based access control policy for granting permissions on resources.

values.name: identity_account
values.description: User account in the identity system.

values.name: api_key
values.description: Credential for programmatic API access.

values.name: invitation
values.description: Shareable link for joining an organization with a configurable role.

values.name: identity_provider
values.description: External identity provider for federated authentication.

values.name: oauth_app
values.description: Registered OAuth application with an external vendor for outbound authentication.

values.name: platform_client
values.description: OAuth2 client credential for platform builders embedding Stigmer into their products.

values.name: organization
values.description:
Top-level tenant that owns and manages resources.

 Organization is the one resource whose metadata.id equals its metadata.slug
 (set by the create pipeline), not a minted org_<ulid>. It is the immutable,
 globally unique tenancy root that every child resource references by slug
 (metadata.org), so its slug is globally unique and doubles as its id.
 id_prefix below is retained deliberately: it still anchors legacy org_<ulid>
 records and the CLI's id-vs-slug detection — it is not used to mint new ids.

values.name: platform
values.description: Singleton platform instance representing the Stigmer deployment.

values.name: agent
values.description: AI assistant with instructions, tools, skills, and a delegation model.

values.name: agent_execution
values.description: Single run of an agent within a session, tracking tool calls and responses.

values.name: session
values.description: Conversation thread between a user and an agent.

values.name: skill
values.description: Knowledge resource that provides domain-specific context to an agent.

values.name: mcp_server
values.description: External tool server connected via the Model Context Protocol.

values.name: agent_instance
values.description: Configured deployment of an agent with environment-specific overrides.

values.name: agent_share
values.description: Hosted chat link for an agent with its own audience, origins, and credentials.

values.name: agent_channel
values.description: Connection binding an agent to an external messaging platform workspace.

values.name: channel_app
values.description:
Customer-owned messaging-platform app (e.g. a Slack app) that agent
 channels can install through instead of the shared platform app.

values.name: workflow
values.description: Multi-step orchestration defining how agents collaborate on a task.

values.name: workflow_instance
values.description: Configured deployment of a workflow with environment-specific bindings.

values.name: workflow_execution
values.description: Single run of a workflow instance, tracking step progress and outcomes.

values.name: environment
values.description: Named set of variables and secrets for agent and workflow execution.

values.name: artifact
values.description: Persisted blob produced during workflow or agent execution.

values.name: execution_context
values.description: User-owned runtime context for managing execution state.

values.name: schedule
values.description: Recurring trigger that runs an agent on a cron schedule.

values.name: project
values.description: Aggregate root grouping related resources for lifecycle management.

enumTypes.name: OAuthConnectionHealth
enumTypes.description:
OAuthConnectionHealth evaluates the health of an OAuth connection by
 examining grant existence and token expiry metadata. Used in
 GetOAuthGrantStatusOutput to give the frontend an actionable signal
 beyond the binary "connected" boolean.

 The backend determines health from locally available metadata (grant
 record + access_token_expires_at). It cannot detect server-side token
 revocation without making an API call to the vendor, so HEALTHY means
 "valid as far as we know" — not a guarantee the token will be accepted.

values.name: OAUTH_CONNECTION_HEALTH_HEALTHY
values.description: The access token exists and is not expired (or does not expire).

values.name: OAUTH_CONNECTION_HEALTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED
values.description:
The access token is expired and no refresh token is available.
 The user must re-authenticate via the OAuth flow.

values.name: OAUTH_CONNECTION_HEALTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED_REFRESHABLE
values.description:
The access token is expired but a refresh token is available.
 The backend will attempt automatic refresh at execution time.
 If the refresh token is itself expired, the refresh will fail and
 the user will need to re-authenticate.

values.name: OAUTH_CONNECTION_HEALTH_NO_GRANT
values.description:
No OAuth grant exists for this resource + org + user combination.
 The user has never connected or has disconnected.

enumTypes.name: ValidationState
enumTypes.description:
ValidationState represents the structural validity of an MCP server definition.
 This is NOT runtime health — it only indicates whether the definition is valid.

values.name: valid
values.description:
The MCP server definition is structurally valid.
 All required fields are present and have valid values.
 The definition can be referenced by agents.

values.name: invalid
values.description:
The MCP server definition is invalid.
 Check validation_message for details on what's wrong.
 The definition should be corrected before use.

enumTypes.name: VendorApprovalStatus
enumTypes.description:
Lifecycle status of an OAuthApp's vendor marketplace approval.

 Vendors like Slack, Figma, and Salesforce require third-party OAuth
 apps to pass a review/approval process before they can be used by
 end users. This enum tracks that lifecycle.

values.name: VENDOR_APPROVAL_STATUS_PENDING
values.description:
The OAuth app has been submitted to the vendor for review and is
 awaiting approval. The sign-in button is disabled in the UI.

values.name: VENDOR_APPROVAL_STATUS_APPROVED
values.description: The vendor has approved the OAuth app. Sign-in is enabled.

values.name: VENDOR_APPROVAL_STATUS_REJECTED
values.description: The vendor rejected the OAuth app. Sign-in is disabled.

enumTypes.name: OAuthAppSource
enumTypes.description:
OAuthAppSource identifies where the effective OAuth app for an MCP server
 was resolved from. Populated at query time by the backend enricher to tell
 the frontend which credential source is active for the current org context.

 Used in OAuthStatus.effective_oauth_source (read-only, not persisted).

values.name: OAUTH_APP_SOURCE_PLATFORM
values.description: The platform-default OAuthApp is in use (McpServerAuth.oauth_app_ref).

values.name: OAUTH_APP_SOURCE_ORG_OVERRIDE
values.description: An org-level BYOA override is in use (OAuthAppOverride binding).

values.name: OAUTH_APP_SOURCE_NONE
values.description:
No OAuthApp is available. The MCP server either uses DCR (mcp_oauth)
 or has no auth block at all.

resourceDescription: McpServer represents a reusable MCP (Model Context Protocol) server configuration.

statusType.name: McpServerStatus
statusType.description: McpServerStatus represents the system-managed state of an MCP server definition.

fields.name: ValidationState
fields.description:
Validation state of the MCP server definition.
 Indicates whether the definition passed structural validation.

fields.name: ValidationMessage
fields.description:
Human-readable validation message.
 Populated when validation_state is INVALID to explain what's wrong.
 Empty when validation_state is VALID or UNSPECIFIED.
 Examples:
 - "server_type is required: must specify stdio, http, or docker"
 - "http.url is not a valid URL: missing scheme"
 - "docker.image is required"

fields.name: DiscoveredCapabilities
fields.description:
Tools and resource templates discovered from the MCP server.
 Optional — absent until the connect RPC has been called (or seeded from seedpack).

fields.name: ToolApprovals
fields.description: System-generated tool approval policies.

fields.name: OauthStatus
fields.description:
OAuth-related enrichment state, populated at query time by the backend.
 Contains vendor approval status (resolved from the referenced OAuthApp)
 and BYOA resolution chain results (which OAuthApp is effective for the
 caller's org context). None of these fields are persisted.

fields.name: Audit
fields.description: Standard audit information (created_at, updated_at, created_by, etc.)

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAudit
statusNestedTypes.description: ApiResourceAudit contains both spec-level and status-level audit details.

fields.name: SpecAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's specification (desired state).

fields.name: StatusAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's status (actual state).

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAuditActor
statusNestedTypes.description:
ApiResourceAuditActor represents the entity that performed an action.

 This is the platform's single actor vocabulary: every "who did this"
 reference (created_by / updated_by, version-history applied_by / pushed_by,
 approval resolved_by_actor) uses this message, so actor rendering is
 uniform across all surfaces.

fields.name: Id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the actor.

fields.name: Avatar
fields.description: URL to the actor's avatar image.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.description:
Human-readable display name (e.g. "Ada Lovelace"). Empty when unknown;
 renderers fall back to email, then id.

fields.name: Email
fields.description:
Email address of the actor. Empty when unknown or not applicable
 (e.g. machine accounts).

fields.name: CreatedBy
fields.description: Actor who created this resource.

fields.name: CreatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was created.

fields.name: UpdatedBy
fields.description: Actor who last updated this resource.

fields.name: UpdatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was last updated.

fields.name: Event
fields.description: Type of the last event (e.g., "created", "updated").

statusNestedTypes.name: DiscoveredCapabilities
statusNestedTypes.description: DiscoveredCapabilities holds the tools and resource templates reported by an MCP server.

fields.name: Tools
fields.description: Callable tools reported by the MCP server.

fields.name: ResourceTemplates
fields.description: Read-only data endpoints reported by the MCP server.

fields.name: LastDiscoveredAt
fields.description: When this snapshot was captured.

statusNestedTypes.name: DiscoveredResourceTemplate
statusNestedTypes.description: DiscoveredResourceTemplate describes a parameterized resource template reported by an MCP server.

fields.name: UriTemplate
fields.description:
URI template with placeholders (RFC 6570).
 Example: "stigmer://agents/{org}/{slug}"

fields.name: Name
fields.description: Identifier for this resource template.

fields.name: Description
fields.description: Human-readable description of the resource.

fields.name: MimeType
fields.description:
MIME type of the resource content.
 Example: "application/json"

statusNestedTypes.name: DiscoveredTool
statusNestedTypes.description: DiscoveredTool describes a single tool reported by an MCP server.

fields.name: Name
fields.description:
Unique tool name within the MCP server (case-sensitive).
 Example: "search", "get_agent", "apply_mcp_server"

fields.name: Description
fields.description: Human-readable description of the tool's purpose.

fields.name: InputSchema
fields.description: JSON Schema describing the tool's input parameters.

statusNestedTypes.name: OAuthStatus
statusNestedTypes.description: OAuthStatus holds system-derived OAuth enrichment state for an MCP server.

fields.name: VendorApprovalStatus
fields.description:
Vendor marketplace/app-review approval status for this MCP server's
 OAuth app. Resolved from the referenced OAuthApp at query time.
 When the platform OAuthApp is pending vendor approval, the frontend
 gates the sign-in button and shows a BYOA alternative.

fields.name: VendorApprovalDocsUrl
fields.description:
Documentation URL for users who want to bring their own OAuth app
 credentials while the platform's OAuth app is pending vendor approval.
 Resolved from the referenced OAuthApp at query time.
 Empty when the OAuthApp has no documentation link or is already approved.

fields.name: EffectiveOauthSource
fields.description:
Where the effective OAuth app was resolved from for the caller's org.
 Computed from the resolution chain:
   1. OAuthAppOverride for (resource_id, resource_kind, org_id) → ORG_OVERRIDE
   2. McpServerAuth.oauth_app_ref → PLATFORM
   3. Neither exists → NONE

fields.name: EffectiveOauthAppId
fields.description:
System-generated ID (metadata.id) of the OAuthApp that the resolution
 chain selected. Empty when effective_oauth_source is NONE.

statusNestedTypes.name: ToolApprovalPolicy
statusNestedTypes.description: ToolApprovalPolicy defines approval requirements for a specific tool.

fields.name: ToolName
fields.description:
Name of the tool (must match tools/list from MCP server exactly).
 Case-sensitive matching against tool names reported by the MCP server.
 Example: "delete_repository", "send_email", "execute_sql"

fields.name: Message
fields.description:
Human-readable message shown to user when approval is requested.
 Supports {{args.field}} placeholders for dynamic content.

 If empty, a default message is generated: "Execute tool: {tool_name}"

 Guidelines for effective messages:
   - Be specific about what will happen
   - Include the most important argument values using placeholders
   - Keep under 100 characters for UI display
   - Use action verbs: "Delete", "Send", "Execute", "Create"

fields.name: FromDestructiveHint
fields.description:
True when the connect-time fail-closed tightener force-gated this tool
 because the server's own MCP annotation declared destructiveHint=true,
 rather than the classifier (or a human) gating it. Lets the runner attribute
 a tightened tool to its true provenance
 (ApprovalPolicySource.APPROVAL_POLICY_SOURCE_ANNOTATION_DESTRUCTIVE_TIGHTEN)
 instead of collapsing it into the classifier default. Carries no enforcement
 weight — gating is decided by presence in this list — so an absent/false
 value simply means "not attributed to the destructiveHint tightener".

 Set only on entries written to McpServerStatus.tool_approvals (the classifier
 layer). It is meaningless on McpServerSpec.pinned_tool_approvals (a human
 pin is, by definition, a pinned override) and left false there.
